feature: Pen points in an icon frame land on whole units
summary: Inside an icon frame every Pen point now lands on a whole pixel, pulled onto a keyline or onto another shape's point when it is near one, with nothing to switch on. A shape drawn that way copies and exports as SVG with whole numbers throughout.
setup: Photonz Dev, release Next, no flag changed from its default. Walk: Scripts/playtest/pen-lands-on-whole-units-in-an-icon-walk.json.

try.do: Choose Layer > New Frame, pick 24 under Icons, then Add Frame.
Zoom in to about 800% so the frame fills a good part of the window.
Press P and click three points roughly, a little off the dashed lines.
try.shotNote: Photographed with the window behind another app, the way a walk leaves it. Blue buttons and picked controls show their background look here; with the window in front they take the accent colour.

try.do: Click the first point to close the shape, then press Esc to drop the pick.
Press P, start a second shape just beside a corner of the first, press and drag for a curve, and hover where the last point goes.
try.shotNote: Photographed with the window behind another app, the way a walk leaves it. Blue buttons and picked controls show their background look here; with the window in front they take the accent colour.

try.do: Click, press Return, pick the frame and press Cmd C, then paste into a text editor.
try.shotNote: Photographed with the window behind another app, the way a walk leaves it. Blue buttons and picked controls show their background look here; with the window in front they take the accent colour.

try.do: Hold Cmd while clicking a point and check it lands exactly where you clicked.

evaluate: Does every point land where you meant it, with no half pixel anywhere in the pasted SVG?
Does the pull onto a keyline or another shape's corner feel helpful at 800%, or does it grab points you wanted one pixel away?
Zoomed right out, is it still possible to place the point you want, or do the keylines take over?
Is the ring under the pointer enough to tell where a point will land, or do you want the place written beside it as the mock shows?
rough: The mock (Draw an icon on the grid, Grid & snap group) has a Snap to row with Grid, Keylines and Geometry; here icon snapping is always on with no row. Task icon-snapping-reaches-what-the-icon-mock-draws.
The mock shows a readout beside the pointer naming the place a point will land (step 4); here there is only the ring. Task icon-snapping-reaches-what-the-icon-mock-draws.
The mock snaps to shapes' edges and centres as well as their points; here only points pull. Task icon-snapping-reaches-what-the-icon-mock-draws.

The mock suspends snapping with Control; the app's key for no magnets is Cmd everywhere on the canvas, and the Pen keeps that. Task icon-snapping-reaches-what-the-icon-mock-draws carries the card for it.
A curve that bulges past its own first point still copies with fractions in its SVG, although every point and handle is whole. Task a-curve-drawn-on-whole-units-exports-on-whole-un.
Only the Pen snaps this way; the rectangle and ellipse tools in an icon frame keep their own magnets.

Right after a shape closes it stays picked, so a Pen press on its corner grabs that corner instead of starting a new shape there. Press Esc first. Noted on task icon-snapping-reaches-what-the-icon-mock-draws.
